public_payload.normalized_proposition: If US courts or Congress held companies liable for their chatbots' output, all LLM providers would be in deep trouble.
conditions: if US courts rule that chatbot output is the company's own speech, or Congress legislates so

statement.excerpt: If American courts were to rule similarly, or if Congress made that the law of the land, all the LLM providers would be in deep, deep trouble.
statement.document_title: Maybe Section 230 doesn’t shield AI companies from liability, after all

from_speaker: If American courts were to rule similarly
or if Congress made that the law of the land
our_interpretation: The antecedent requires an operative US ruling or enacted federal law treating provider-generated chatbot output as the provider’s responsibility in the relevant liability context.
A complaint, proposed bill, or procedural refusal to dismiss does not alone establish that antecedent.
Read “deep, deep trouble” as serious adverse legal or operational consequences, rather than merely exposure to a lawsuit.
Retain the claim’s universal scope. Harm to one provider cannot establish harm to all.
criteria.support_condition: After a qualifying legal event, evidence establishes serious adverse liability consequences across the claimed provider population.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent is established, a decisive legal event makes the universal consequence impossible, such as a controlling exclusion that permanently removes an included provider from the relevant liability exposure.
